notes.title: Second Annual Welcome to Freedom Town 3-Gun Tournament
notes.notes:
It's that time of year again, Shooters! Get ready for the [i]Second Annual Range is HOT!™️ Welcome to Freedom Town 3-Gun Tournament[/i]. This year, we have 3 new courses for the tournament.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/05X1OxX.png[/img]

You will have 2 chances to compete on each course. We are not locking away new courses before participating in the tournament this time 'round, so make sure to run through the new courses beforehand to give yourself the best chance of topping the leaderboard.

The tournament will run June 23rd through July 25th.

In addition to new courses, the entire game has undergone some major optimization.  This several month effort should have courses loading faster and give higher framerates across the board.  Also, you may notice, two of the new courses are in a new indoor environment.

For all of you content creators out there, a new option has been added for configuring the output on your monitor! 

You can select which eye is displayed so spectators can properly see down your sights. 
[img]https://media2.giphy.com/media/QdSiwc6QtvV7lh7jTN/giphy.gif?cid=790b76110e5e61fc3f641460a9261d827c6d14763182c15b&rid=giphy.gif&ct=g[/img]

The field of view can be adjusted to show more or less of the environment around you. 
[img]https://media3.giphy.com/media/RLbflp3aO91iEJuU9d/giphy.gif?cid=790b7611e52b32e1777a4fbd08b31ea3927bd9e9e8f3b5c1&rid=giphy.gif&ct=g[/img]

There are position and rotation smoothing options to reduce the jittery look of head movement. 
[img]https://media0.giphy.com/media/J1TTBCHFiwFQCE6h5u/giphy.gif?cid=790b7611369f94b09d2f5f5bec56aed9e7c31143046e857e&rid=giphy.gif&ct=g[/img]

[img]https://media1.giphy.com/media/978KwPOVeOHgjK1sWz/giphy.gif?cid=790b7611f2a439331af85ebbf49c3f1ae2825c80f6a48f5f&rid=giphy.gif&ct=g[/img]

Finally, the roll of the camera can be disabled. 
[img]https://media1.giphy.com/media/qWM3GUparIkvXFhOeo/giphy.gif?cid=790b761182329dc888f4014048f91ef8477312af40184825&rid=giphy.gif&ct=g[/img]

All of these features can be tweaked to make for a much more pleasant viewing experience! 

Be warned - this level of customization is only possible by using an additional camera, which means everything gets rendered twice. It looks great, but comes with a big performance cost.

We're not exactly pros at [url=https://www.twitch.tv/winterbearstudio]the whole streaming thing[/url], but if you want help getting yourself set up to stream your Range is HOT!™️ gameplay, hop on over to our [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] and we'll help you the best we can.

    Thanks and good luck in Freedom Town!
   -The Range is HOT!™️ team

notes.title: State Of The Game 9/22/21
notes.notes:
It's been a while since the last SOTG.  Partly due to a string of smaller updates to the game, and partly due to a (personal) bout with Covid.  But all is well, and if you've been keeping up with the game on your own, we think you'll agree we've been busy!

[h3]New Firearms[/h3]
Last week we launched the DaviDae S320 pistol.  It looks great and comes with the full suite of optics available in the loadout screen.  We haven't seen any negative feedback so far on it, but if you've got something to say about it, hop over to the [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] and let us know how to improve.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/zf7VCk0.png[/img]

This week, we've got another one for you.  We're not sure how many shooters will choose to run it in our current courses, but hey, how many different shotguns can you really make?  We also wanted to set a challenge for ourselves to tackle the mechanics of a pump action.  Look for the Fossberg 500 in this weeks update, then as always, head over to the [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] to let us know what you think of it.  

[img]https://i.imgur.com/5KCsmfZ.png[/img]

If you've been following our Friday Night Dev Streams ([url=https://www.twitch.tv/winterbearstudio]Twitch[/url], [url=https://www.youtube.com/c/WinterBearStudioLLC]Youtube[/url], [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/WinterBearStudio]Facebook[/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1503590/Range_is_HOT/]Steam[/url]), you've probably seen much of the recent updates, as well as the discovery of the issues that lead to these updates.  If not, subscribe, follow, or just hop in the chat Friday nights at 8:30pm MST to get the very latest.  
[h3]Fixes/Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Updated Red Dot for visibility
[*] Adjusted audio fall off range for steel targets
[*] Changed failure to engage penalty to just be 5 seconds per infraction
[*] Swingers stop swinging upon course completion
[*] Adjustments to table colision to prevent wacky gun bouncing
[*] New Target Variations with no-shoot occlusion
[*] Added option to disable visual activators on the Trap/Skeet range
[*] Added reminders to Classifiers 09-02 & 13-01 for facing uprange
[/list]
[h3]New Courses
[/h3]
WBPSA Classifiers:
[list]
[*] 19-03
[*] 19-01
[*] 20-01
[*] 20-02
[*] 09-02
[*] 13-01
[/list]
3Gun Courses:
[list]
[*] Fast Act 01
[*] Fast Act 02
[*] Fast Act 03
[*] Fast Act 04
[*] Fast Act 05
[/list]
[h3]Course Editor[/h3]
We thought we'd gather a bunch of the assets together to give you an idea of what we're playing with for the editor.  None of these assets are guaranteed to make it to the final editor, but heres a bunch of stuff we're trying to get working.

Obviously, you'll need these to make a functioning course...
[img]https://i.imgur.com/24JaFKp.png[/img]

And here's some mesh barriers we want to make available...
[img]https://i.imgur.com/Akos9bb.png[/img]

Some barriers that obstruct line of sight...
[img]https://i.imgur.com/0BZO7xA.png[/img]

Some props to dress things up...
[img]https://i.imgur.com/q0uBLP1.png[/img]

Some walls for those indoor courses...
[img]https://i.imgur.com/l71JX15.png[/img]

And of course, targets...
[img]https://i.imgur.com/qdWhKEg.png[/img]

...lots of targets
[img]https://i.imgur.com/oEGpmNN.png[/img]

This is what we're working with so far.  If you think we're missing something, or have ideas you'd like to see added, the only way we'll know about it is if you head over to (you guessed it) our [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] and bring it up.  The whole dev team is there, as well as a great community of gamers and real world shooters.  Together, we think we'll be able to make something really powerful.

As far as rolling all of this out, we're thinking about doing this in phases, the first of which would actually be a [i]range editor[/i].  Some time ago, we added an internal feature to add shooting ranges to the game that aren't bound by the rule sets of the various competitions, and we think this should be our first vertical slice we tackle.

After rolling out Ranges, we'll want to tackle the problem of sharing and browsing these courses.  This might be rough in our first implementation.  There's a number of things to try here.  We've made progress on converting our courses to be data driven, and at the early stages of sharing we may just be sending eachother big ol' walls of text, or maybe we'll do some sort of workshop integration.  

After implementing sharing, we'll move on to rolling out the different rule sets.  There's a number of challenges to take on to get this stuff working.  How do we let shooters lay out shooting lanes?  How do make the ropes work?  How do we make sure scoring is automatically handled?  What kinds of things need to be restricted so the editor doesn't become some sort of nightmare experience where shooters need a 4 year degree to understand it?  How do we tutorialize this thing so it doesn't annoy shooters who "get it" but doesn't frustrate shooters who don't?

One feature we're designing around is making sure you can easily swap between editing and playing the course you're working on as seen in [i]Halo[/i]'s Forge and [i]Mario Maker[/i].  This ability to build, test, build, test, etc... without saving and loading at every turn makes all the difference in usability and is really something we want.  And of course we want all of these tools to be in-game.  You won't need to learn Blender or Unity to make courses, and of course, you'll be making courses [i]in[/i] VR.

Do you know of any games with built in level editors we should be looking at for inspiration?  Do you have ideas that may answer some of our toughest questions?  Is there a glaring hole in our plans?  Again, head on over to the [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] and let us know!

Thanks,
12 Gauge Savior

notes.title: State Of The Game 8/04/21
notes.notes:
Since the last State of the Game two weeks ago (sorry 'bout that, Shooters), we've added some pretty great stuff to the game.

First off, we've added a new course, Fox Hole 06, which has designated shooting zones.  We hope you like it as much as we do.  We've also added 3 new WBPSA courses, 06-01, 06-02, and 06-04.  We dig 'em and we'll be adding more in the coming weeks.

We've also added a new firearm, the Grizlikov 80 (GK-80).  This is our modernized AK pattern rifle, built for competition for the shooters that just can't accept AR pattern rifles being the go-to platform for 3Gun.  It accepts all the current optic attachments, so you can still run your LPVO with an offset Red Dot if you like.  It also supports the "classic" AK reload.  We'd like some feedback on how this feels, so come sound off in the [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord [/url] and let us know how we did.

There's also a couple of Quality of Life improvements.  The Leaderboard now has a "Self" tab where you can view your 10 best personal scores.  We've been tracking them the whole time, so this should be populated the first time you look at it.  We've also added a configurable dead zone to the movement input.  Feedback was positive on this improvement to aiming (and therefore toggling the safety), so we brought it over to the movement input as well.  This may help those unfortunate shooters who don't have dedicated thumbsticks.

The vanishing magazine bug should be fixed, or at least we finally found a reliable way to reproduce the bug, and have since squashed the bug.  Let us know if you still see any disappearing mags, especially if you can make it happen reliably.

Lastly, work is continuing on the upcoming p320 pattern pistol.  This was by far the most requested pistol in our Firearms Survey, so we're taking our sweet time and gettin' it right.

If it's been a while since you've hopped in game, you should give it a go.  Steady progress has been made and we're now up to 36 3gun Courses, and 10 WBPSA Classifiers!  There's a couple new guns and plenty of courses to try them out on.

Thanks,
12 Gauge Savior

notes.title: State Of The Game 7/21/21
notes.notes:
It's been a while since we posted a simple State of the Game!  There's a lot going on behind the scenes, so let's get to it.

First off, there was another new course added last week, Fox Hole 05.  This course has defined firing boxes, which is something we haven't done on the past few.  It's a cool challenge, be sure to check it out!

We've been working on implementing Open XR for some time now, and it's getting close.  Open XR is the cutting edge of input handling. Every platform is pursuing it, so it's the best path for ongoing support from XR providers. It also makes adding support for new controllers relatively trivial.  Since controllers will have a more universal input interface, it makes in-game customization simpler to implement, which is also something we've been talking about for a while.

Open XR has a couple of other advantages as well, for example, rendering will have a more universal interface, which should mean more reliable rendering on every platform.  There are likely to be some growing pains, but the sooner the standard is adopted the sooner we can work out those kinks.  Users will want to make sure they're using the XR provider that is best for their platform. Each platform has their own way of setting the provider.

In general, this should help us improve the game in the future, for example:  Oculus and SteamVR have unique orientations for the hands. Because of that we had to detect the active platform and apply an additional rotation to the hand models to get them to properly align in each platform to accommodate their arbitrary reasoning. OpenXR has a standard for hand rotations, so that check is no longer needed.  This also means if we add some kind of user calibration to hand rotation, it's far simpler to apply such a setting going forward.

All this tech work doesn't mean the Art Team have been taking a nap.  After wrapping up the assets for the last tournament, work began on a couple of new guns.  First off, we have out P320 clone in progress.  Obviously there is a lot more detail that needs to be added, but it's coming along.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/giYS28w.png[/img]

And here's an early look at our AK pattern rifle...

[img]https://i.imgur.com/1IErIEu.jpg[/img]

Don't like em?  Think Open XR is dumb?  Love the new course?!  Come join the whole Dev Team on our [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord [/url]and join the conversation!

Thanks,
12 Gauge Savior

notes.notes:
This week we added a new Dog Avenger course, bringing action targets to our fast paced set of courses.  This rounds out the courses so each themed section has at least one course with moving targets.

We've also added the tech for multi-string classifiers, bringing in two of these for shooters to test and give feedback on.  Do they work?  Do they make sense? notes.title: The High Country Update
notes.notes:
It's time for a change in scenery.  We're going from the high desert to the high country.  We love our original range, loosely modeled after a local range located in rural Colorado, but it's easy to get tired of the dry desert and it's time to get up into the Rockies.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Y0G4sjC.png[/img]
Situated in the forest, within the shady pines, this range builds on feedback from our shooters and leverages what we have learned building courses so far.  More verticality and versatility were a couple goals, as well as something that's simply visually different.  This range isn't modeled after any range we've been to, it's more like what we'd build if we had a plot of land on the mountainside, and a bunch of machinery to carve and shape it to our vision of a fun place to shoot.

Our first course on this new range is featured in the First Annual High Country Hootenanny 3-Gun Tournament.  This tournament is the first of many, challenging shooters to run 3 courses with only one chance to compete on each.  No retry, no reset, make Every. Shot. Count.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/WJJjCmz.png[/img]
Once you've participated in the tournament, you'll be able to replay the course on the new range.  The course will stay locked until you've completed it in order to preserve a course that shooters are not allowed to do scored practice runs ahead of the tournament.  You will be able to walk the course and formulate a strategy before your scored run in the tournament.  Rest assured, we'll be adding more courses to the new range after the tournament concludes.  The High Country Hootenanny will happen May 21st through May 30th.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/6ncGa64.png[/img]
Each tournament will run for a limited time, giving shooters a chance to participate at their convenience.  Once you have finished your runs, you'll want to keep checking back to see how your results stack up against the shooters that are finishing theirs.  

[img]https://i.imgur.com/qOr3cf4.png[/img]
Once the tournament has concluded, shooters will be awarded medals for placing 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place, as well as top 10, and top 50.  As we run more tournaments, we'll add a place to see your accomplishments and a way to show your prowess to other shooters.

The High Country Update rolls out Friday May 21st.

    Thanks and good luck in the Hootenanny!
   -The Range is HOT! team

notes.title: State Of The Game 5/19/21
notes.notes:
We had to delay our build last week by a couple days, but the update rolled out this Monday and brings the new render pipeline to the game.  A couple things might look a little different, the Shoothouse for example, but we're still working on it.  This pipeline brings some minor performance improvements and a new graphics setting, allowing you to toggle SSAO on or off.

We added an experimental setting allowing users to customize their Interpupillary distance (IPD) setting.  If your optic doesn't seem to be lined up where it should be, give this a tweak.  We are trying to set everyone's IPD automatically, so you should only mess with this if you're seeing noticeably wonky optic alignment.

Speaking of optics, we've added some flip-up iron sights as the "no optic" option on the Rifle.  It was a little weird having a naked rifle as an option.  We're unsure how useable these will be because of resolution being a challenge in general on most headsets, we'd really appreciate some feedback on what shooters think.  Head on over to our [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] to let us know what you think.

On the UI side of things, we fixed attachment icons not displaying properly on the loadout screen.  Not really sure how or when this broke, but hey, it's fixed.  We also unified the player menu course list, loadout screen, and the tournament screen into one cohesive UI.  This will be a nice feature when you participate in a tournament, allowing you to change your loadout based on which course you are about to attempt.

And on the topic of Tournaments, a placeholder UI has been added for tournaments in the latest build, but we're still iterating on it internally over the next couple days, in a effort to get it polished up for launching this feature in the next build.  This tournament will feature 3 courses, one of which is brand new, in a brand new environment.  This course will not be available to play until you participate in the tournament.  Shooters can of course walk the course before you do your run, but you will not have an opportunity to do scored practice runs.

When the new build rolls out, look for the High Country Hootenanny tournament.  Tournaments are a custom leaderboard where you only get one chance to log a score, similar to our Friday night Developer Streams we've done over on our [url=https://www.twitch.tv/winterbearstudio]Twitch[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/c/WinterBearStudioLLC/videos]Youtube[/url] channels.  You only get one chance so make Every. Shot. Count!

Thanks,
12 Gauge Savior

notes.title: State Of The Game 5/12/21
notes.notes:
Classifiers are starting to feel like a "real mode".  We've added starting positions with a visual aid to let you know where to put your hands to start the run.  Procedural penalties have been added, so scoring should be pretty accurate, and the 180° rule is now being enforced.  We also fixed and adjusted some of the classifiers, like a target being in the wrong position on Classifier 03 or that you could just walk through the button pedestals.

Last week we added a new smart ammo snapping feature to belts.  This was initially well received in the [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url], however, some shooters don't like it, so this week, we're adding an option in the player menu to disable it.

On the Quest, we're still trying fixes for the double fire issue.  If you're still seeing this, we could use your help in tracking down a way to reliably reproduce it.  On the Index side of things, we've added an option to set the safety toggle to the touchpad, or click the joystick, or both.  This should give the option to take the stress off of those thumbsticks for those who are concerned about longevity.

This week, we're working on switching to a different rendering pipeline.  This is something we want to get done now so we can build with it in mind going forward.  It's a big task and might not be finished this week, but hopefully this will give us more to work with in terms of scaling the game to different platforms, more knobs to turn for performance, and just a better looking game.

Also this week, we are running our first tournament internally.  We've still got some UX things to polish up, but it's working, the leaderboard for it is working, and we're discovering the obviously broken things so our shooters don't have to.  We know we've been talking about it for awhile but we are passing these last few bumps and its looking really good we will be having our first tournament next week.

Thanks,
12 Gauge Savior

notes.title: State Of The Game 5/5/21
notes.notes:
Our practical shooting mode is coming along.  Scoring is now presented as hit factor, which is based on points earned divided by time.  We're also getting more rules in place, so some procedural penalties are now being detected, such as shooting no shoots, extra shot/hit for Virginia rules, etc.  Practical shooting has a lot of rules, so standby as we get all of these in.  The 180° rule should be coming in this week's update, and will be applied to the WBPSA practice classifiers, so stay safe out there!

We have a new movement option available in the settings, you can now set your player movement to be relative to your controller instead of your headset.  This may help some of you perform reloads while moving better.  In our experience, it takes a lot of practice to get used to.

Our shooters come in all shapes and sizes, and now, so does our belt!  We're still making tweaks, and this week we've added some rotational snapping to allow easier grabbing of attachments specific to the firearm you're holding.  Remember, you can position things on your belt where you like, so open up that menu, get it set up for yourself, and then hop in the [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] to tell us what you think.

Progress is moving along with Tournaments internally.  We're hoping to be able to test locally next week, and get a tournament rolled out for everyone the following week.  There's like a million things that could go wrong, so standby for updates on that timeline.

Finally, I want to thank the shooters that popped in our live stream last Friday.  We're getting more comfortable with it, having more fun, and it's great to have some live interaction with our [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] users.  You can find replays of our stream on our [url=https://www.twitch.tv/winterbearstudio]Twitch Channel[/url].

Keep the feedback comin',
12 Gauge Savior

notes.title: State Of The Game 4/28/21
notes.notes:
We're going to try a new streaming schedule to make our Fridays less hectic.  We're planning on doing a brief State of the Game stream Wednesday afternoon, and then move our usual developer play sessions later on Fridays, shootin' for 8pm.

We've changed the gun belt up a bit to make it more usable.  Now the belt snaps to your hands to help get to the things you're trying to grab, and no-look grabbing has been vastly improved.  We're still working on improvements here, so test it out and leave feedback in the [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url].

We've noticed some accidental double tapping with Oculus controllers, so we've added a system to combat that behavior.  Unfortunately, immediately after updating the live build, we got reports that some users are still experiencing this problem, so if you can [i]reliably reproduce[/i] this, reach out to us on [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] and let us know your experience, we obviously need to dig deeper.

We've started adding classifier practice courses to the game.  These are modeled off of real world courses used to group real world shooters into classes so they can compete against similarly skilled shooters.  We are planning on adding as many of these as we can, and also setting up the full ruleset so shooters can practice and learn the stages, without the cost of ammo, of course.

Practicing these courses requires some tools though, so we've added a shot timer to them.  Like a real world belt mounted timer, ours will give you a "shooter ready?  ...standby   ...beep" count, and then show you shot times and splits.  We hope this will make these practice stages usable to shooters who are interested in competing and can compliment (not replace) dry fire practice while we all patiently wait for ammo availability.  For now, you'll have to walk the course and call your own hits and misses, but we'll be adding those rules and scoring in the coming weeks.

Now the stinky part.  The backend for our new tournament system is taking longer than we'd like, but we need to get it right in order for tournaments to function properly.  This means the tournament events will be delayed until (likely) the end of May.  We're sorry for the delay, but we want a good, reliable backend, especially to prevent any kind of janky tournament features. We'll get it right ...standby.

Thanks,
12 Gauge Savior

notes.title: State Of The Game 4/20/21
notes.notes:
While we're pushing forward on bringing Tournament Events to the game, we're also working on a couple other things.  You may have noticed a change in the UI, reorganizing some things to hopefully make it less overwhelming.  We're looking for feedback from shooters as to how this feels.  We know we're not done with it yet.

We also implemented our optimizations to terrain.  This really shouldn't be a noticeable change, but it needed to be done because we're working on a new environment, which means we needed to adjust our art pipeline first.  I'm happy to say the new environment looks amazing and is a welcome change of scenery.  The first course developed in this new environment is a blast, and we feel like it's a culmination of everything we've learned building courses so far.  Can't wait to see what you think.

While we're spinning up our new leaderboard system we're also cooking up a couple other things for our competitive shooters.  We've started modelling out a few Practical Shooting classifier courses.  We won't really have a Practical Shooting [i]mode [/i]right away, but we figured it'd still be useful for shooters to be able to practice on them.  We'll be adding more classifiers in the coming weeks, so please be patient, but feel free to sound off in the [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] about which courses are most useful to you.

So, without an actual [i]mode[/i], how helpful can Practical Shooting classifiers really be?  Well, a lot more helpful with the other new feature coming this week.  We're adding a shot timer to these courses.  No, it's not gonna be some little blue box on your belt, it's going to use some of the tech we've already got to accomplish this.  Each classifier course should have a shot timer UI panel near the start that will show times and splits.  You'll have to inspect your targets to call your own Alphas and Mikes, but we think it'll still be a useful practice tool.

There's a lot of game rules that need to be implemented to support the real world versions of these types of courses: strong and weak hand shots, ammo limits and classes, and things like mandatory magazine changes to name a few.  It's a bit much to bite off in a single week of development, but we figured adding this shot timer would allow shooters to practice the way they would IRL, and give us a bit of room for the art team to keep developing these courses while the programmers navigate the gigantic rule book.

As we continue building out these features, we can't stress how valuable feedback is.  Our shooters have guided most of our decisions and we will be leaning heavily on our [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] community, so get in there and let us know what you think.

Thanks,
12 Gauge Savior

notes.title: State of the Game 4/13/21
notes.notes:
While there hasn’t been a bunch of content added to the game in the past couple weeks, we have been hard at work fixing things up, squashing bugs, and laying groundwork for upcoming features.  We’ve added more robust graphics settings, allowing you to tweak settings for Detail, Shadows, Anti Aliasing, and Post Processing.  Shooters on our [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] have reported these settings enabling them to achieve smoother performance and higher frame rates, so if your setup is struggling a bit, give ‘em a shot.

Another performance improvement should be coming later this week.  If we’ve done our job right, you really shouldn’t see any visual difference, but after some experimentation, we’ve decided to handle terrain a bit differently.  This new terrain should be indistinguishable from the old terrain, but shooters with older GPUs might notice slightly better framerates.

Now that we’ve added some courses that have ammo and mag limits, we quickly realized dropping a magazine accidentally was pretty much cause to restart the course, so we’ve changed it so magazines and shot shells do not automatically disappear during your run.  This also means magazines can be picked up and placed back in their belt slots.  Also, the shot shell caddy now has slots.

We love seeing videos of shooters’ runs, sometimes we’re just in awe of the raw speed we see, and sometimes we say “Hey c’mon, man” and see something we feel we need to address.  So, we’ve added more recoil when shooting the long guns one handed.  Our apologies to those trying to live out their [i]Arnold in Predator[/i] fantasies.

We’ve squashed a lot of bugs, check patch notes for the full list, but the big offenders were poppers not resetting properly, a discrepancy in the reporting of times in certain edge cases, and a crash that would happen when reholstering the pistol.

There’s also a number of small tweaks to things such as the game automatically using the Oculus runtime if you’re using an Oculus, picking a color for the red dot, renaming a few things in the loadout UI, an adjustment to to smacking the bolt release on the WBR 15 (formerly called the MSR), adjustments to the orientation of hands across all platforms, and Index controllers can now use the touchpad to toggle the safety.

Vive controls have had a number of tweaks.  Movement swipes can now begin anywhere on the touchpad.  Buttons can now be clicked anywhere in their quadrant, not just the edge, and you shouldn’t have issues accidentally triggering two button presses, like toggle safety and magazine ejection.  Let us know how this stuff feels to you, we’re still listening.

We’re finally revamping the UI.  This will be rolled out in stages, first looking at size, scale, and anchoring, then looking towards a cleaner layout.  We’ve already revamped the backend of the system so now the art team can hammer out the rest as we move forward.  You may notice we’ve sort of been piling on stuff, just getting it in and working as we add features, and we are currently developing some more UI to support the new Event System we are implementing.  In the meantime, the pointer in the UI has been updated to be a little more natural to use, and later this week, we’re hoping to have some improvements as well.

Wait…  New Event System?!  Yup.

We’ve been building out a new backend for leaderboards.  It’s a big change and takes some time, but it’s going to support our new update, Tournaments!  Tournaments will be limited time events where we pick a few courses, set a timeframe, and give you [u]one chance[/u] to log a score for each course.  We know that allowing shooters to just hammer run after run on the same course leads to highly optimized times, and we wanted something a little more true to life.  As you may have seen on our live streams, results can wind up different when you are limited to one run.  More pressure.  No retries.  Make every shot count.

Along with these new events, we want a change of scenery, so we’re moving from the high desert up into the high country.  We have a new environment in the works and we can’t wait to show it off.  We have a couple goals with this new environment.  Obviously, we want some much needed variety in environments, but additionally, we’re taking everything we’ve learned building our current courses and giving ourselves a little more variety in layout.  This doesn’t mean we won’t be designing new courses in our original setting, but the next few courses will definitely happen here.

So, when is this new stuff coming?  Well, we don’t exactly know, but we’re targeting the end of April/beginning of May.  We certainly don’t want our first tournament to be a disaster, so testing not only the systems, but the user experience as well, will dictate the exact time as we approach the end of the month.

Finally, we’re looking forward to participating in the next Steam Sale.  We don’t get notified when these sales are happening until they’re about to happen, but it’s been a while and we’re hoping there’s some sort of sale coming in the next month or so.

So, if you know someone who is holding out for a discount on the game, or maybe a friend who wants a little more variety, tell them to wishlist the game, and let 'em know there's something coming soon.

Thanks,
12 Gauge Savior

notes.title: State of the Game 3/30/21
notes.notes:
We've added five new courses, and we can't wait to hear your feedback on them.  They pretty much all incorporate some sort of magazine or ammo limit, which we think is a welcome change of pace, and a new level of challenge.

We saw some big movement on the leaderboards this past Sunday, you might need to hop in-game and check to see if your scores are safe (well, as safe as they can be in early access).  This sparked some ideas in the team that we can hopefully talk about soon.

The basic weapon loadout is in, you can now swap some of the existing optics around, and set up the offset for either right or left hand shooters.  This will be used in the future as we add more types of attachments, and more guns to the game.

Grounding barrels will now be more forgiving and hopefully feel more natural during a run.  This should mean no more unexpected behavior when grounding your long guns, no more ruined runs because of wonky physics.  Speaking of physics, there is now the ability to throw items, which should nothing for your run, but make handling objects a little less immersion breaking.

Lastly, we've upgraded the version of Unity we're using, which allows us to explore the new Open XR standards which is necessary for the input rewrite.

This coming week, we're focusing on mostly technical stuff and polish.  Unfortunately, this means we'll be  lite on new content, but we can't put this stuff off any longer.  We need to get some of these things off our plate so we can move forward without nagging issues.

Best,
12 Gauge Savior

notes.title: State of the Game 3/23/21
notes.notes:
We’ve added a couple new “Dog Avenger” courses.  One is a 3 gun course and one is Rifle only.  A shotgun only, and pistol only course are in the works as well.  These are intended to be fast paced, less movement courses, hopefully giving you that Hollywood training feel.  Pro Tip: You can shoot through paper targets and hits on multiple targets count.  We’re expecting low leaderboard times and high replayability, but as is true with all of our efforts, we want to know what you think about these.

We’ve also added over under shotguns to the shotgun practice course.  We think they’re pretty classy, and an important step towards full Skeet and Trap modes.

The offset red dot has been added to the MSR.  We’re already making a color adjustment to the default dot color, and are discussing ways to let shooters pick right-side or left-side setup, as well as dot color.  Apologies to our southpaw shooters, but we wanted to rush this in.  Left-side setup is coming.

On the topic of lefties, a southpaw movement option has been added to the control options.  This is a hotfix while we rewrite our input system to support as many devices as possible.  More updates to control options will be coming in the following weeks.

Fixing grounding barrels has bubbled to the top of our list this week.  They should be vastly improved over their previous iteration.  They’ll still look like the same old barrels, but now we shouldn’t have screwy physics happening while you're in the heat of your run.  The goal here is reliability, so you can dump it and move on with your run.

We’re working on getting the loadout UI in.  We’re not going fancy with it, but we want to give you options and give ourselves the ability to work with attachments without rewriting the codebase every time our artists make a cool weapon accessory.

On top of fixing more bugs, we’re also going to try to add a couple new courses, because more content is a message well received from our community.

Lastly, thanks to the shooters that joined us on Discord for our first Developer Stream.  It was a bit rough, but we had fun anyway, and are all looking forward to doing it again in the future.

Thanks,
12 Gauge Savior

notes.title: State of the Game 3/16/21
notes.notes:
It’s been a week since we’ve launched on Early Access and things are already HOT!  We count ourselves lucky that we have a very positive community growing on our [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]official Discord[/url].  The conversations there have been a great mix of feedback and suggestions from both gamers and real life competitive shooters.

With the help of last week’s survey on the [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url], our priorities are pretty clear.  First, we have to get controls right for everyone.  Second, we need to tackle performance.  Obviously, both of these are issues that don’t affect every shooter, but we don’t want to leave anyone behind.  Then, the fun part, CONTENT!  The demand for a Course Editor is clear, and we’ll be picking that back up as soon as possible, but some groundwork needs to be laid.  The Course Editor will definitely be our longest-term effort, based on what’s on our plate right now, so we ask for a little patience to get it right.

Controller support has been a serious challenge.  It’s been a mix of hot fixing what we have so more people can play and give us feedback, as well as a longer term rewrite.  Controllers without joysticks (Vive and some WMR) are particularly tough to manage as we need a certain minimum number of inputs to maintain the interactivity with the guns and allow the courses to be playable.  So, we’re rewriting the system, exposing more options to players, and continuing to tune touchpad inputs as best we can.  This effort might take a couple/few weeks, but we’ll continue to put quick fixes in where we can.  Movement options for left handed shooters should be coming in this week’s update.

A note on WMR, there isn't really an option to handle WMR input without having WMR hardware on hand. There's a simulator for the standard WMR controller, but outside of that there's not a whole lot we can do until we acquire relevant hardware. OpenXR might solve this sooner, but we'll have to try out upgrading Unity version to use that, which of course has the potential to break other things, so, testing, testing, and more testing.

Performance will always be an ongoing problem as we make new content, but we’ve identified a couple major offenders and are tackling one big one this week.  The level environments.  They are consuming too many resources and we are actively attempting different tools and approaches to see how much we can reduce their consumption. Sadly, do not expect an immediate change this week on this. We'll keep you guys updated as this progresses.

Our feedback has identified a few issues with our UI such as usability and comfort, so this effort will be a little bigger, and will be an iterative process over the coming weeks.

We’re having a lot of fun with the Aerial Clays Practice range, and are adding a new gun to really sell the experience.  It feels weird to be busting clays with a 8+1 capacity shotgun with a big ol’ mag tube hanging off the front, so a new over/under break-action shotgun is in the works.  It’s something we really want to have to bring the upcoming Trap and Skeet modes to life in a way that invites more shooters to our game.

Speaking of new game modes, the survey has spoken and we’re going to tackle new modes sooner rather than later.  We’ll be leaning on the [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url] group heavily as the 120 page rule book for USPSA is a bit daunting, but hopefully with your help, we can get a first course up and running and then flesh out the massive list of options after we get one nailed down.  While most of the tasks detailed above can be handled by one team member putting their nose to the grindstone, this USPSA mode will be both a team AND community effort.  

We also need to lay some groundwork for loadouts.  We’re not going to have a ton of options right away, but we need some way to set up and configure the new offset red dot!  We’re expecting this to dramatically increase usability in shorter range rifle scenarios such as inside the Shoot House B&B.

Some new assets are in the works inspired by a certain tactical training school known for training a certain Hollywood action star on gun handling for a certain series of movies loved by shooters and gamers alike.  We’re also going to use this opportunity to design a course that is shorter and more stationary than the courses that involve a lot of movement.  Dog Avengers, make ready!

I plan on keeping this S.O.T.G. a weekly feature on our Steam page.  We really do want this game to be a community driven experience, and so far, it seems to be working.  We’re also planning a Developer Stream for this Friday 3/19/21 @ 5:00pm Mountain Time on the [url=https://discord.gg/CdNZHCUyHC]Discord[/url], we hope you’ll join and make fun of our terrible shooting.

Finally, I wanted to thank everyone for giving our game, and our team, a chance.  Your feedback and suggestions have been invaluable in guiding our decision making process.  To that end, there will be another survey coming soon specifically asking about courses and their design in Range is HOT!

Thanks,
12 Gauge Savior
